sample_unit: exposure hierarchies (72 GPT-5 and 18 expert-generated) rated by blinded experts

links.outcome: Blinded expert ratings of GPT-5 vs clinician-created ERP hierarchies on matched vignettes
links.effect: No significant differences except variability, where experts scored higher (P=.02; r=0.24). Raters identified the AI hierarchy in 17/54 pairs (31.5%), below chance.
links.quote: GPT-5 generated ERP hierarchies for BDD that blinded experts rated as comparable to clinician-created hierarchies and could not reliably distinguish them from clinician-created hierarchies.

links.outcome: Expert-rated safety and quality of AI hierarchies, by patient insight level
links.effect: Overall ratings high (means 4.39-4.90/5), but absent-insight hierarchies had lower safety (P<.001; r=0.73) and overall quality (P=.01; r=0.43). Exposure difficulty miscalibration was the most common rater concern (30/43 comments).
links.quote: Insight level was the most consistent predictor of quality: absent-insight hierarchies received significantly lower safety (P<.001; r=0.73) and overall quality ratings (P=.01; r=0.43).

unlisted_practices: Blinded expert rating of AI-generated therapy content against clinician-created content

screen.reason: The study empirically assesses the quality and safety of LLM-generated exposure hierarchies across simulated BDD clinical vignettes compared to expert clinicians, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
